title: Import Data

vrt.dialogDescription: Combine multiple raster datasets into a single virtual layer.
vrt.mosaicHelp: Combines multiple rasters into a single continuous layer. Sources are spatially arranged side-by-side. All sources must share the same CRS, data type, and band count.
vrt.bandStackHelp: Stacks multiple single-band rasters into a multi-band dataset. Each source becomes one band. Sources must have identical grid dimensions and resolution.
vrt.resFinestHelp: Uses the highest resolution (smallest pixel size) among all sources. Other sources are resampled to match.
vrt.resCoarsestHelp: Uses the lowest resolution (largest pixel size). Faster but loses detail from finer sources.
vrt.resAverageHelp: Uses the mean resolution across all sources. Balances detail and performance.
vrt.gridMismatch: Grid dimensions do not match (width, height, or resolution differs)

upload.hintEncoding: Try saving the file with UTF-8 encoding
upload.hintGeometry: Check that the file contains valid geometry data

reservedRename.title: Reserved column names renamed
reservedRename.description: Source columns that clash with GeoLens-internal column names were automatically renamed with a `src_` prefix so both the source data and pipeline geometry can coexist.

dbfTruncation.title: Shapefile field name collisions
dbfTruncation.description: Shapefile DBF field names are capped at 10 characters. Two or more source fields collapsed to the same truncated name and may have been merged during import.

mercatorClip.title: Geometry outside the Web Mercator bounds
mercatorClip.description: GeoLens serves Web Mercator tiles, which cover longitude -180° to 180° and latitude -85.06° to 85.06°. Geometry outside that box was clipped away during import. The rows are still in the dataset; only their geometry changed. Check both the coordinate order and the coordinate range of your source.
mercatorClip.skippedDescription: The source coordinate system has a narrow area of validity, so the Web Mercator bounds could not be expressed in it and the boundary check was skipped. No geometry was removed, but geometry outside longitude -180° to 180° or latitude -85.06° to 85.06° may still be present and will not render on the map.
mercatorClip.clipped_one: {{count}} feature was trimmed at the boundary
mercatorClip.clipped_other: {{count}} features were trimmed at the boundary

archiveFailed.title: Original file archive failed
archiveFailed.description: The dataset was imported successfully, but copying the original source file to durable storage failed. The dataset is still queryable; re-upload if you need the original file restored.

temporalParseErrors.title: Temporal fields dropped
temporalParseErrors.description: The following temporal values could not be parsed as ISO-8601 dates and were dropped. Re-enter them in the dataset metadata editor to restore them.

complete.heroDesc: All files ingested, tiled, and indexed. Ready to query, style, and map.

serviceUrl.label: Service URL
serviceUrl.placeholder: https://example.com/wfs, ArcGIS FeatureServer, or OGC API endpoint
serviceUrl.helpText: Paste a WFS, ArcGIS Feature Service, or OGC API Features URL
serviceUrl.noLayers: No layers were found in this service.
serviceUrl.tokenPlaceholder: ArcGIS token, API key, or WFS access token
serviceUrl.credentialHelpText: Choose the method your service documents. A bearer token is sent as an Authorization header; a username and password are sent as HTTP Basic auth; an API key can go under whatever header name the provider specifies — for example X-API-Key, Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key, or key.
serviceUrl.authMethodSignin: Sign in with username and password
serviceUrl.authMethodToken: Paste a token or API key
serviceUrl.arcgisTokenHelpText: Use an API key if your account can create one; Viewer accounts and accounts using single sign-on or multi-factor authentication can't. Otherwise, generate one from your portal's Sharing API with client=referer. Tokens last at most 15 days.
serviceUrl.arcgisSigninFailed: Failed to sign in to ArcGIS
serviceUrl.signinHelpText: Signing in mints a token valid for 60 minutes; an import that runs longer will need a new one. This won't reach a portal on a private network, so paste a token instead if yours is private.
serviceUrl.arcgisTokenExpiredMidImport: Your ArcGIS sign-in expired while this was open. Go back and sign in again to continue.

urlImport.label: File URL; fetched server-side
urlImport.fetchingHint: Large files can take several minutes to download; keep this page open.
urlImport.filenameHelpText: Only needed when the URL path doesn't end in the file name; for example a download link keyed by an id.
urlImport.fetchFailed: Failed to fetch the file from that URL
urlImport.previewFailed: Failed to analyze the downloaded file

rail.stageDesc: Drop or pick files. No commit yet; you can remove any before detection.
rail.reviewDesc: Confirm geometry type, CRS, schema, and preview for each file.
rail.importDesc: Tile, index, publish; datasets appear in the Catalog immediately.
rail.vectorDesc: tiled to MVT, spatial index, reprojected to 3857 on read.
rail.rasterDesc: converted to COG, overviews built, bands kept intact.
rail.tableDesc: ingested as a joinable table. Optionally specify geometry columns during import.
rail.tipText: Drop multiple files at once to create a batch. Each file becomes its own dataset; you can review and adjust metadata before committing.
rail.registerDesc: Register existing PostGIS tables as datasets; GeoLens tiles them on the fly from your database.
rail.stacDesc: Connect a STAC catalog or collection and import selected assets into GeoLens.
rail.serviceDesc: Connect a remote WFS, ArcGIS FeatureServer, or OGC API Features service. GeoLens imports the layer into the catalog for tiling and querying.
rail.registerNote: No data copied · tiles generated directly from your tables
rail.stacNote: STAC metadata is discovered first, then selected assets are imported
rail.serviceNote: Service tokens are used for this import and are never stored with the dataset
rail.compareRegister: Upload ingests from a file. Register points at an existing table; no duplication, but the table must stay in your database.
rail.compareStac: Upload ingests local files. STAC imports discover remote assets first, then stages selected items for catalog use.
rail.compareService: Upload ingests from a file. Service URL fetches from a remote API and imports the data into GeoLens for local tiling and querying.
rail.urlDesc: GeoLens downloads the file server-side into staging, then runs the same detection and import pipeline as an upload.
rail.urlNote: The URL is validated and size-capped before download · data is copied into GeoLens
rail.compareUrl: Upload sends a file from your machine. File URL fetches it from the web; same review, same result, no local download needed.

register.helpText: Catalog existing PostGIS tables from your database as datasets in GeoLens. Use this when you have geographic data already in the database that wasn't imported through GeoLens. Selected tables will be added to the dataset catalog with automatic metadata detection.
register.emptyState: No unregistered tables found in the database.

emptyStateAllRegistered.title: All PostGIS tables are already registered
emptyStateAllRegistered.body: Every spatial table in your database is wired up as a GeoLens dataset. To add new data, use the Upload File tab or import from a Service URL.

emptyStateNoTables.title: No spatial tables found
emptyStateNoTables.body: The database has no registrable PostGIS tables. Upload a file or import a service URL to start building your catalog.

register.selectHint: Select a table from the list to see its schema and register it.
register.detailDesc: Register to expose as a GeoLens dataset; tiled on the fly, no copy.

layerPicker.title: Select Layer

metadata.compressionHelp: COG output compression. DEFLATE is default. ZSTD for speed, JPEG/WEBP for imagery.

metadata.nodataHelp: Override or assign a nodata value for this raster.
metadata.embeddedGeometryHelp: This source already includes native geometry, so GeoLens will keep it during import.
